status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should provide meaningful information making stakeholders aware of interactions with AI, including workplace interactions.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Section 1.3(ii) is used as a nonbinding AI-awareness benchmark for the operators and recipients of the reported 2025 synthetic financial/public-official advertisements. AI-mediated interaction scope and period are established without a binding duty or certification claim.
previous_canonical_assessment.finding_basis: False recognizable endorsement and a fraudulent solicitation are evidenced, but the full advertisement/interface and recipient-specific AI-awareness disclosures are not preserved. Misrepresented endorsement is distinct from whether meaningful information about AI interaction was supplied; the taxonomy failure does not automatically decide that information proposition.

review.reason_for_change: The advertisements presented synthetic likenesses and voices as genuine financial or government endorsement. Their subjects and recipients were not meaningfully informed of the AI impersonation.

review.requirement_proposition: Protect vulnerable users, require specific consent for bounded deceptive styles, document emergent deception and define safeguard-failure protocols.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: A fraudulent YouTube advertisement used an AI-generated likeness and voice of Western Australian Premier Roger Cook to promote an investment scheme as government-backed. IEEE 7014.1-2026 applies to partner-based GPAI systems using emulated empathy in human-AI partnering contexts. These sources describe synthetic videos/advertisements impersonating real people, not an empathic AI partner interacting with a user; they also do not describe personal or emotional data collection by such a partner system. The required system context is absent.

review.reason_for_change: The 2025 campaign predates the represented 2026 partner-interaction source version.

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: The campaign used recognisable people’s likenesses without authority to solicit investment under a false endorsement. This did not respect the portrayed people’s identity or recipients’ agency. It does not establish every downstream consequence.

review.requirement_proposition: Add intended purpose, nominal operator and responsible contact information to the public documentation.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: IEEE-7001 Table 2 level 3 (Add intended purpose, nominal operator and responsible contact information to the public documentation.) requires the relevant autonomous-system stakeholder level or ethical-design process and undertaking. The sources do not establish that context; firsthand impersonation or correction evidence does not prove full conformance. Only admitted metadata is used.

review.reason_for_change: A generated impersonation advertisement is not the autonomous-system identification object governed by these requirements.

review.requirement_proposition: Parties must ensure adequate transparency requirements tailored to the context and risk of AI lifecycle activities, including identification of AI-generated content.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 8 concerns Parties and implemented territorial lifecycle/transparency/rights duties. Relevant entry into force, implementation covering the private actor and the occurrence trigger are not established; official fraud warnings or an internal editorial policy do not supply treaty applicability.

review.reason_for_change: These provisions address treaty Parties and implementation measures, not the fraudsters’ own disclosure duties.

review.requirement_proposition: Do not apply affective modeling to identifiable subject data without prior informed consent.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: A fraudulent YouTube advertisement used an AI-generated likeness and voice of Western Australian Premier Roger Cook to promote an investment scheme as government-backed. The IEEE 7014-2024 clause applies when affective modeling is applied to identifiable subject affective data. The source evidence describes synthetic identity/voice portrayals for advertising; it does not describe affective modeling of the depicted person's affective data. The clause's data-processing condition is absent.

review.reason_for_change: Synthetic likeness and voice are reported, but no affective modelling of identifiable subject data is established.

review.requirement_proposition: Make the system clearly identifiable as autonomous to users and bystanders.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: IEEE-7001 Table 2 level 1 (Make the system clearly identifiable as autonomous to users and bystanders.) requires the relevant autonomous-system stakeholder level or ethical-design process and undertaking. The sources do not establish that context; firsthand impersonation or correction evidence does not prove full conformance. Only admitted metadata is used.

review.reason_for_change: A generated impersonation advertisement is not the autonomous-system identification object governed by these requirements.

review.requirement_proposition: Parties must seek to ensure that people interacting with AI are told they are interacting with a system rather than a human, as appropriate to the context.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 15(2) concerns Parties and implemented territorial lifecycle/transparency/rights duties. Relevant entry into force, implementation covering the private actor and the occurrence trigger are not established; official fraud warnings or an internal editorial policy do not supply treaty applicability.

review.reason_for_change: These provisions address treaty Parties and implementation measures, not the fraudsters’ own disclosure duties.

review.requirement_proposition: Do not place, put into service or use AI that deploys subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques causing materially distorted behavior and significant harm.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The source establishes that a synthetic false endorsement appeared in an Australian YouTube advertisement and was publicly rejected by the Premier and Consumer Protection Commissioner. It does not establish whether the AI output was used in the Union, whether a relevant provider or deployer placed or used the system in the Union, or where the responsible actors were established. It also does not establish the advertisement's reach or other facts needed to determine whether significant harm was reasonably likely. Those unresolved territorial and harm conditions prevent an occurrence-level applicability conclusion.

review.reason_for_change: The campaign predates the represented July 2026 source version. The source record does not independently resolve all actor, territory and harm conditions of the prohibition.

review.requirement_proposition: Minimise data and make review, modification and withdrawal of consent immediate and accessible.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: A fraudulent YouTube advertisement used an AI-generated likeness and voice of Western Australian Premier Roger Cook to promote an investment scheme as government-backed. IEEE 7014.1-2026 applies to partner-based GPAI systems using emulated empathy in human-AI partnering contexts. These sources describe synthetic videos/advertisements impersonating real people, not an empathic AI partner interacting with a user; they also do not describe personal or emotional data collection by such a partner system. The required system context is absent.

review.reason_for_change: The 2025 campaign predates the represented 2026 partner-interaction source version.

review.requirement_proposition: Document interactions with GAI systems to users prior to interactive activities, particularly in contexts involving more significant risks.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST-AI-600-1 GV-5.1-002 (Document interactions with GAI systems to users prior to interactive activities, particularly in contexts involving more significant risks.) is a voluntary organization/lifecycle action. The the November 2025 Roger Cook synthetic advertisement establishes no adoption or full action-specific incident-plan, escalation criteria, contact procedure, TEVV, provenance, metrics or bias programme. A target intrusion, public notification or corrected dispatch does not establish that independent applicability.

review.reason_for_change: The source identifies a published advertisement, not an interactive GAI activity with users to which this prior-interaction documentation requirement applies.

conclusion_change.previous: The advertisement treated a synthetic representation of a public official as carrying the official's actual endorsement authority. The incident materialised impersonation and correction burden, while financial harm remains attempted rather than established. Unauthorized official portrayal, false economic endorsement and engineered trust retain distinct failures. The public warning establishes attempted solicitation and correction burden, without realized victim loss or model-initiated intent.
conclusion_change.new: The synthetic advertisements falsely conveyed investment endorsement and concealed AI impersonation. The reported identity and agency failures are assessed separately from later framework versions. No realised victim loss is established.
